extracted.intended_audience: taxonomists, field zoologists, and naturalists studying freshwater bryozoa (Plumatella, Stolella) and museum curators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and exemplar diagnostic criteria for describing and identifying freshwater bryozoan species (genera Plumatella, Stolella and related taxa), emphasizing morphological characters (zoarium, zooecia, statoblasts, polypide), distribution, types and biology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zoarium characters (growth form & branching)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the zoarium: whether recumbent, adherent, dendritic, cushion-shaped, sack-like, linear, spreading over large surfaces, radiate or dichotomous, whether branches are far apart or pressed together, and presence/strength of vertical branches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use observations such as 'zoarium in the typical form has a loose appearance due to the fact that the branches are far apart', 'often covers a considerable area on flat surfaces', 'entirely recumbent', 'adherent and linear', 'branches freely and at short intervals in a horizontal plane', and note how substrate or overgrowth (e.g., sponges) affects zoarium form (examples: P. fruticosa, P. emarginata, P. diffusa, P. tanganyikæ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of branching (pattern & topology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the branching method: lateral, dichotomous, radiate, sparse lateral branching, linear series, fan-like formation, or formation of root-like rhizome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish patterns such as dichotomous branching (two young zooecia diverging from a mother-zooecium), lateral and irregular branching, linear series without lateral branches, and radiate arrangements when crowded on stems. Diagrams and comparative remarks (e.g., fig. 43) are used to convey characteristic patterns (P. emarginata vs P. javanica vs Stolella).

rubrics_metrics.name: Zooecia morphology (shape, length, orientation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe zooecia shape (cylindrical, L-shaped, elbowed, stout, slender, short and broad, constricted at base, tapering toward orifice), their usual orientation (upright, recumbent), and whether they are packed with statoblasts in particular limbs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete comparisons: e.g., 'zooecia are cylindrical and bear a simple keel', 'great majority are L-shaped, the long limb being usually adherent' (P. diffusa), 'short and broad; their base is always recumbent' (P. tanganyikæ). Note how shape distinguishes species (P. diffusa vs P. allmani).

rubrics_metrics.name: Zooecia surface features (keel, furrow, emargination, annulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record dorsal keel presence and conspicuousness, furrowing, emargination at the tip, and external annulation or tuberculation of the ectocyst.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example phrases: 'bear a simple keel on their dorsal surface', 'emarginate or furrowed', 'conspicuous furrowed keel', 'conspicuous, although often irregular external annulation' (P. tanganyikæ), 'not emarginate or furrowed' (P. punctata). These features are diagnostic and often compared across species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ectocyst attributes (thickness, rigidity, pigment, texture, transparency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the ectocyst: thin or thick, rigid or soft, hyaline/transparent or pigmented/dark/colourless, rough or smooth, tuberculate, swollen and contractile, glassy or polished, with annulations or rings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note statements such as 'ectocyst is thin and never very rigid', 'ectocyst is stiff; colour usually pale pinkish brown', 'hyaline and as a rule absolutely colourless' (P. javanica), 'swollen, soft ectocyst which can be transversely wrinkled...and is distinctly contractile' (P. punctata). These characters are repeatedly used to separate taxa and to explain environmental staining effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statoblast characters (free vs fixed, shape, size, swim‑ring, capsule, air-cells)
rubrics_metrics.description: Document presence/absence of free and fixed statoblasts, their frequency, outline (elongate, truncate, broadly oval, circular, rhomboidal), relative proportions (length vs breadth), capsule size, swim-ring morphology (extent over dorsal surface, free portion breadth), air-cell distribution, surface reticulation or tuberculation, and membranous margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use detailed metrics and descriptions given: e.g., 'free statoblasts are at least considerably, sometimes very elongate', 'capsule is relatively large and resembles the swim-ring in outline', 'free statoblasts are variable and often asymmetrical', 'fixed statoblasts have a solid margin instead of a swim-ring and are often minutely serrated'. Differences in statoblast form are emphasized as key diagnostic characters across species (P. fruticosa, P. emarginata, P. diffusa, P. tanganyikæ, P. punctata).

rubrics_metrics.name: Polypide anatomy (tentacle number, velum, stomach shape)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record number and character of tentacles, presence and extent of the velum at their base, velum/tentacle projections or tubercles, and stomach shape (slender, elongate, stout, rounded base, abruptly truncated posteriorly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'tentacles number between 40 and 50 and are not festooned at the base' (P. fruticosa), 'lophophore bears 20 to 30 tentacles...velum extends up each tentacle in the form of a sharply pointed projection' (P. tanganyikæ), 'polypide comparatively short and stout' (P. punctata). Tentacle counts and velum morphology are used as diagnostic features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal structure: partitions, rhizome and basal elongation
rubrics_metrics.description: Note presence/absence and character of internal partitions (their number and stoutness), formation of rhizome or root-like tubes by elongation of basal parts, and embedding of basal parts in substrate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use statements like 'internal partitions are numerous and stout', 'root-like tube...formed by the great elongation of the basal part of a zooecium' (Stolella), and 'base often seems to be actually embedded in the support' (P. tanganyikæ). Such internal features affect colony shape and genus-level diagnosis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seasonality, habitat and biological associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Document the species' habitat preferences (ponds, stones, plants, stems of bulrushes, floating logs), seasonal occurrence (cold-weather species, rains), salinity tolerance (slightly brackish), and associations with other organisms (sponges, rotifers, duckweed, social rotifers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include 'always grows near the surface or near the edge of water', 'essentially a cold-weather species in Calcutta', 'often found together with Stolella indica', and observations that sponges can compress zooecia causing coralloides forms. Biology entries also include reproductive timing (e.g., fixed statoblasts in old colonies nearing hot weather).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical distribution and collection localities
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide documented geographical range, specific localities (cities, provinces, lakes), and altitudes where specimens were taken; indicate probable wider distribution when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit locality lists and altitude notes such as 'I have seen Indian specimens from the Punjab (Lahore), from Bombay, from Travancore, from Calcutta...from Kurseong in the E. Himalayas (alt. 4,500 feet)', and remarks about occurrence in Europe/N. America/Africa. These data support biogeographic and identification judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types and museum repositories
rubrics_metrics.description: Record whether type specimens exist and where they are housed (e.g., Hamburg Museum, Indian Museum, Philadelphia Academy of Sciences) or note 'type not in existence'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state 'TYPE not in existence' or 'TYPES in the Hamburg and Indian Museums', and cite which named types were examined or provided by other workers. Type information grounds taxonomic decisions and comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic remarks and comparative diagnosis
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the species with closely allied taxa, note distinguishing characters, enumerate phases/varieties and gradations, and give differential diagnoses tying morphological differences to species limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include comparative language used in the text: e.g., 'closely allied to P. repens but always has much longer statoblasts', 'three phases of the species may be distinguished', 'closely allied to P. philippinensis but the latter has a smooth and polished ectocyst'. Use these comparative remarks to justify species delimitation and to caution about environmental modification of characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Larval and reproductive development details
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe larval form, ciliation, pore, timing of polypide development inside statoblasts, mode of settlement and budding to form a new polyparium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt descriptions like 'minute pear-shaped, bladder-like body covered externally with fine vibratile threads (cilia) and having a pore at the narrow end', 'at the period it is set free it already contains a fully formed polypide or pair of polypides', and developmental sequence 'settles down on broad end...polypide is everted through the pore...a fresh polyparium rapidly formed by budding.' These developmental traits are diagnostic and inform life-history notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field/collection tip: using animal constructions as samplers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use incidental or observational collection guidance such as examining the tubes of other animals (e.g., the worm Aulophorus tonkinensis) to survey presence of statoblasts, sponges and phylactolæmata in a pond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by the text: 'I know of no better way of obtaining a general idea as to what sponges and phylactolæmata are present in a pond than to examine the tubes of Aulophorus tonkinensis.' Such tips are practical adjuncts to formal morphological criteria for surveying local fauna.
